questions.q: L-asparaginase is given by ____ route.
questions.exp: Route: I/V (Book p290)

questions.q: L-asparaginase is selectively lymphotoxic because it:
opts: Breaks down asparagine, which lymphocytes cannot synthesize
Blocks asparagine uptake by all cells equally
questions.exp: Breaks down asparagine (blocks source to lymphocytes); lymphocytes cannot synthesize asparagine → selective lymphocyte toxicity; use ALL (Book p290)

questions.q: Match the ↓ protein effect of L-asparaginase to its consequence.
questions.exp: ↓insulin → hyperglycemia; ↓lipoproteins → hyperlipidemia; ↓coagulation factors → hemorrhage; ↓anti-coagulation factors → hypercoagulation (Book p290)

questions.q: The last listed L-asparaginase side effect is ____.
questions.exp: S/E d/t ↓ protein + hypersensitivity (Book p290)

questions.q: In PML, the RARα gene sits on chromosome ____ and translocates to chromosome 15 (PML gene).
questions.exp: RARα gene chromosome 17; PML gene chromosome 15 → translocation (Book p290)

questions.q: DOC for PML is ____ ; if unresponsive: arsenic trioxide.
questions.exp: Use: DOC for PML; unresponsive → arsenic trioxide (Book p290)

questions.q: Retinoic acid's side effect is ____ syndrome.
questions.exp: Side effect: pulmonary syndrome (Book p290)

questions.q: Retinoic acid acts as a ____ agent at ↑ dose (supra-physiological levels).
questions.exp: Acts as differentiating agent at ↑ dose (Book p290)

questions.q: The proteasome inhibitors used in multiple myeloma are bortezomib and ____.
questions.exp: Bortezomib, carfilzomib — multiple myeloma (Book p291)

questions.q: Proteasome inhibitor S/E: thrombocytopenia and ____.
questions.exp: S/E: thrombocytopenia, peripheral neuropathy (Book p291)

questions.q: The four-drug multiple myeloma note: bortezomib + lenalidomide + dexamethasone + ____.
questions.exp: Bortezomib + lenalidomide + dexamethasone + daratumumab (Book p291)

questions.q: Match the monoclonal antibody type to its structure/suffix/example.
questions.exp: Humanised: hypervariable mouse, -zumab, trastuzumab; chimeric: variable mouse, -ximab, abciximab; murine: entire, -omab, ibritumomab; human: entire, -umab, adalimumab (Book p291)

questions.q: Match the MAb nomenclature stem to its target area.
right: Toxin (bezlotoxumab vs Tox-B of C. difficile)
questions.exp: -tu/-tum tumor; -ci/-c circulation; -li/-lim lymphocyte; -tox toxin (Book p291)

questions.q: Match the remaining MAb facts.
right: Via hybridoma (multiple myeloma cells fused in mouse)
questions.exp: -os osteoporosis; -vi virus; synthesis via hybridoma (Book p291)

questions.q: Match the EGFR/HER2 strategy to its drugs.
questions.exp: EGFR receptor: cetuximab/panitumumab; EGFR TK: gefitinib/erlotinib NSCLC; HER2 receptor: trastuzumab (main)/pertuzumab; HER2 TK: lapatinib/neratinib (Book p292)

questions.q: VEGF blockers (bevacizumab, ranibizumab, aflibercept) are used for ____.
questions.exp: VEGF blocked by bevacizumab, ranibizumab, aflibercept — use: macular degeneration (Book p292)

questions.q: VEGFR is blocked by ____ (use: GIT cancer).
questions.exp: VEGFR blocked by ramucirumab (use: GIT cancer) (Book p292)

questions.q: Match the VEGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor to its use.
questions.exp: Vandetanib medullary thyroid; axitinib/sunitinib RCC; sorafenib DOC HCC; lenvatinib RCC & HCC (Book p292)

questions.q: CD20 blockers: rituximab (CLL, NHL, RA); ofatumumab covers CLL and ____.
questions.exp: Ofatumumab: CLL, multiple sclerosis (Book p292)

questions.q: The PD1 blockers listed are:
questions.exp: PD1 blockers: nivolumab, dostarlimab, cemiplimab, pembrolizumab (Book p292)

questions.q: The CTLA4 inhibitor listed is ____.
questions.exp: Ipilimumab: CTLA4 inhibitor (Book p292)

questions.q: PDL1 blockers are durvalumab, avelumab and ____.
questions.exp: PDL1 blockers: durvalumab, avelumab, atezolizumab (Book p292)

questions.q: ICP uses: lung/uterine/bladder Ca & Hodgkin's get pembrolizumab or nivolumab; breast Ca gets ____.
questions.exp: Breast Ca: pembrolizumab (Book p293)

questions.q: PDL1 on normal/cancer cells binds ____ on the lymphocyte, hiding cancer cells from differentiation recognition.
questions.exp: PDL1 binds PD1 on lymphocyte; PDL1 prevents differentiation of normal from cancer cells (Book p292)

questions.q: CTLA4 blocks the APC's ____ , preventing APC from attacking cancer cells.
questions.exp: CTLA4 blocks CD80/86 → prevents APC attack (Book p292)

questions.sec: Bruton's TK, MAPK, Hedgehog and PI3-K
questions.q: Bruton's tyrosine kinase inhibitors: ibrutinib and ____.
questions.exp: Ibrutinib, acalabrutinib (Book p293)

questions.sec: Bruton's TK, MAPK, Hedgehog and PI3-K
questions.q: BTK inhibitor B-cell cancers: CLL, mantle cell lymphoma, marginal zone lymphoma and ____ macro­globulinemia.
questions.exp: Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia (Book p293)

questions.sec: Bruton's TK, MAPK, Hedgehog and PI3-K
questions.q: Match the MAPK-pathway inhibitor group.
questions.exp: BRAF: vemurafenib/dabrafenib/encorafenib; MEK: trametinib/selumetinib/binimetinib; melanoma: 1 BRAF + 1 MEK inhibitor (Book p293)

questions.sec: Bruton's TK, MAPK, Hedgehog and PI3-K
questions.q: Glasdegib (hedgehog blocker) is for elderly (>75 yr) ____ intolerant to normal chemotherapy.
questions.exp: Glasdegib: elderly (>75 yr) AML intolerant to normal chemotherapy (Book p293)

questions.sec: Bruton's TK, MAPK, Hedgehog and PI3-K
questions.q: Sonidegib treats skin cancer — ____ carcinoma.
questions.exp: Sonidegib: skin cancer (basal cell carcinoma) (Book p293)

questions.sec: Bruton's TK, MAPK, Hedgehog and PI3-K
questions.q: Match the PI3-K blocker (and one hedgehog drug) to its add-on use.
questions.exp: Alpelisib: breast with fluvestrant; idelalisib/duvelisib: CLL; sonidegib: basal cell carcinoma (Book p293)

units.title: L-Asparaginase
units.guide: IV; breaks down asparagine (lymphocytes can't synthesize) → selective toxicity; ALL. S/E d/t ↓protein: hyperglycemia, hyperlipidemia, hemorrhage, hypercoagulation; hypersensitivity.

units.title: Retinoic Acid
units.guide: PML: RARα (chr 17) ↔ PML (chr 15) translocation → weak RARα → ↓retinoic acid → immature myeloblasts. DOC PML (unresponsive → arsenic trioxide). S/E pulmonary syndrome. Differentiating agent at supra-physiological dose.

units.title: Proteasome Inhibitors
units.guide: Bortezomib, carfilzomib — multiple myeloma; S/E thrombocytopenia, peripheral neuropathy. Myeloma regimen: bortezomib + lenalidomide + dexamethasone + daratumumab.

units.title: MAb Types and Nomenclature
units.guide: Humanised -zumab (trastuzumab, hypervariable mouse); chimeric -ximab (abciximab, variable mouse); murine -omab (ibritumomab); human -umab (adalimumab). Stems: -tu tumor, -ci circulation, -li lymphocyte, -tox toxin, -os osteoporosis, -vi virus. Synthesis via hybridoma.

units.title: Targeted Therapy: Receptors and TKIs
units.sec: Targeted Therapy: Receptors and TKIs · p292
units.guide: EGFR receptor cetuximab/panitumumab (head-neck/colorectal); EGFR TK gefitinib/erlotinib (NSCLC). HER2 receptor trastuzumab (main)/pertuzumab; HER2 TK lapatinib/neratinib. VEGF blockers macular degeneration; ramucirumab GIT; vandetanib medullary thyroid; axitinib/sunitinib RCC; sorafenib DOC HCC; lenvatinib RCC+HCC. CD20: rituximab, ofatumumab (CLL/MS).

units.title: Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors
units.guide: PD1 blockers: nivolumab, dostarlimab, cemiplimab, pembrolizumab. CTLA4: ipilimumab (blocks CD80/86). PDL1 blockers: durvalumab, avelumab, atezolizumab. Uses: lung/uterine/bladder/Hodgkin's; breast pembrolizumab. PDL1 binds PD1.

units.title: Bruton's TK, MAPK, Hedgehog and PI3-K
units.sec: Bruton's TK, MAPK, Hedgehog and PI3-K · p293
units.guide: BTK ibrutinib/acalabrutinib → B-cell cancers (CLL, mantle, marginal zone, Waldenstrom). MAPK: BRAF vemurafenib/dabrafenib/encorafenib + MEK trametinib/selumetinib/binimetinib → melanoma. Hedgehog: glasdegib elderly AML; sonidegib basal cell. PI3-K: alpelisib breast+fluvestrant; idelalisib/duvelisib CLL.
